memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You have declared this day that the Lord is your God and that you will walk in obedience to him, that you will keep his decrees, commands and laws — that you will listen to him." — Deut 26:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here we come to the heart of the whole chapter — a covenant declaration. The people had declared something that day: the Lord is their God. And that declaration came with commitments — to walk in His ways, to keep His commands, to listen to His voice. Choosing God as your God is never a casual thing; it shapes how you live.

To say "the Lord is my God" is to say far more than "I believe He exists." It is to give Him the throne of your life. It means His ways become your ways, His voice becomes the voice you follow. You cannot claim Him as God while ignoring what He says.

This is a searching question for us. Have we truly declared the Lord as our God — not just with our lips on a Sunday, but with our lives every day? Is He the one we listen to and walk with?

The gospel makes this even richer. We do not walk in obedience to earn God's love, but because He first loved us and gave His Son for us (1 John 4:19). Declaring "the Lord is my God" is our joyful response to grace. And notice — the very next verse shows God making a declaration back over His people. Ours is never the first word; His is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I truly made the Lord my God — over my whole life?
2. Does my daily walk match the declaration of my lips?
3. Am I genuinely listening to God's voice and following it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are my God. I want not only to say it but to live it — walking in Your ways and listening to Your voice. Thank You that I obey in response to Your love. Amen.
